review_type: Independent scoped transaction code, provenance and verification review
approved_scope: Prepare a write-once bound intent at the exact baseline; permit the separately authorized apply_patch to install only the already approved exact candidate; complete a write-once application receipt only after actual canonical candidate, export and guarded historical replay checks succeed. The executor itself does not write canonical YAML.

repair_during_review.finding: Initial historical_view accepted exact baseline despite an existing completed application, leaving an unrecorded rollback undetected.
repair_during_review.resolution: Reviewed executor rejects baseline with existing APPLICATION and validates transaction provenance when INTENT exists even while canonical remains baseline.
independent_negative_checks: Baseline plus completed application rejected with rollback-record requirement.
Baseline plus stale prepared-intent executor binding rejected as provenance drift.

assessments.package_bindings: Exact baseline and candidate digests, pinned independent judgment bytes, all judgment input pins and all frozen-preflight pins are verified before substantive checks. Optimized Python is rejected because the frozen preflight uses assertions.
assessments.review_and_ledger_bindings: Transaction review must explicitly approve and match every binding() field, including current executor bytes. Prepared intent remains required even when application exists; both ledger statuses are checked, both bind exact review bytes, and completed application binds exact intent bytes.
assessments.historical_replay: The outer view substitutes only the exact approved Jeremiah target with its pinned baseline; the existing Numbers helper supplies its separately guarded baseline. Unknown Jeremiah bytes and symlinked canonical targets fail. All other inputs pass through unchanged, and frozen selector reproduction plus context hashes detect unrelated drift. Actual current corpus digest is recomputed outside the Jeremiah overlay.
assessments.exports: The real complete Jeremiah exporter is exercised for actual, baseline-overlay and candidate-overlay views. Restoring only target export content makes candidate and baseline books identical, and candidate verse output must equal the frozen preflight. Completion additionally requires actual export to equal candidate export.
assessments.lifecycle: Preparation requires exact canonical baseline and no prior intent/application. Completion requires intent provenance, exact canonical candidate and successful post-application checks. Existing receipts cannot be overwritten; the reused writer uses exclusive creation, symlink-parent checks and fsync. Baseline after a completed application is now refused.
assessments.canonical_write_boundary: No canonical writer exists in this executor. The separate apply_patch must use exact approved bytes; completion is verification after that operation, not permission for additional verse changes.

independent_validation.read_only_check: PASS: exact baseline; frozen candidate preflight reproduced; 11 dossier contexts reproduced; historical selection and all 101 review contexts reproduced; full actual Jeremiah export has 1364 verses and matches baseline; all other exported book content unchanged.
independent_validation.test_jeremiah_note_transaction: PASS: 21 tests, including actual pins, unknown-state refusal, missing/stale provenance, ledger states, intent-byte binding, historical read restoration, concurrent target change, write-once lifecycle and failed-export refusal.
independent_validation.test_unflagged_english_sample: PASS: all 4 migrated tests against guarded historical replay.
independent_validation.repair_specific_checks: PASS: independently exercised repaired rollback and stale-preparation branches using virtual reads without canonical writes.

limits: This approval binds the exact executor digest above. Further executor edits invalidate it.
Historical checks reproduce prior experiments; they do not certify edited verses under old review scores.
The check and local exporter do not establish deployed reader behavior or constitute publication approval.
The separate source-evidence judgment remains limited to the approved note, anchors and connected metadata; no new source-selection or whole-verse assessment is added here.
